summary: Careful, preregistered paired study with strong artifact grounding and appropriate preregistration fidelity. Primary preregistered inferential null result (exact two‑sided McNemar p=0.0625) is reported and labeled correctly; exploratory one‑sided analyses are explicitly flagged. Execution, accounting, and analysis artifacts appear complete and internally consistent. Remaining publication‑quality defects concern manuscript presentation: the References section must be formatted as a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography using the archived bibliographic records, and the Disclosure Statement must be condensed to the concise mandatory elements (while preserving the immutable master‑prompt locator+SHA‑256 and preregistration identifier). Also tighten one brief Results/Discussion paragraph to make the inferential hierarchy (the primacy of the preregistered two‑sided McNemar) unambiguous.
critical_issues: References section is not presented as a conventional IEEE‑style numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata for each cited work; current identifier‑style or partial entries are not acceptable for the proceedings.

The Disclosure Statement still reads longer than the concise mandatory disclosure required by the track. It must be condensed to a short paragraph that preserves only the required items (declared model(s) and provider(s); orchestration/validator names; immutable initial master prompt locator and exact SHA‑256; preregistration identifier and affirmation it was frozen before model calls; and a statement that no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock).
required_revisions: Replace the References section with a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography using the archived terminal_bibliographic_records (include authors, title, venue/repository, year, and DOI/URL when available). Do not leave bare DOI/arXiv/OpenAlex identifier entries.

Condense the Disclosure Statement to a single concise paragraph that (a) declares the model(s) and provider(s), (b) names the orchestration/validator (hosted_netops_gvr_v1 / deterministic_netops_validator_v5), (c) includes the immutable initial master prompt locator and its exact SHA‑256 (provenance/master_prompt.txt : 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba), (d) states the preregistration identifier (cand‑003‑stud‑001) and that it was frozen prior to any model calls, and (e) affirms that no human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Remove execution/accounting numbers, per‑episode logs, artifact paths, and other archive bookkeeping from the manuscript Disclosure Statement (those belong in the archived evidence bundle).

Revise the Results/Discussion to include one concise paragraph (can be ≤3 sentences) that plainly states the inferential hierarchy: the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test is the confirmatory analysis and it did not reach two‑sided α=0.05 (p=0.0625); the paired bootstrap CI and any one‑sided McNemar reported are descriptive/exploratory and do not overturn the preregistered confirmatory null. Explain in one sentence why the bootstrap CI may exclude zero in the presence of very sparse discordant counts (this explanation can be drawn from the archived analysis_log.jsonl and paired_contingency_table.csv).
optional_revisions: Optionally include a short one‑paragraph boxed appendix or a single small table listing the five discordant pairs (pair IDs and brief failure reason codes) to illustrate repair modes; this can be populated from terminal_factual_accounting and archived artifacts.

Optionally expand Threats to Validity by one short sentence clarifying whether the very high baseline validity likely reflects generator behavior, corpus characteristics, or validator permissiveness and point to which archived artifacts a reader could inspect to adjudicate among those possibilities.
